description: Focused Type-4 positive and hard-negative case handles used by target packets, smoke gates, verifier runs, and regression tests.

hard_negative_groups.claim: Numeric clamp admission must keep bound-order, numeric-domain, shape, and library/API identity hard negatives beside every positive bridge.

Python loop/all plus De Morgan admission must keep vacuous truth, short-circuit timing, helper-call purity, iterator identity, boolean value-context, predicate-coordinate, and effect-safety hard negatives beside the positive packet.

Collection membership admission must keep receiver API/domain proof, searched-element coordinates, collection/source coordinates, and mutation closure beside every literal, factory, imported, or typed dynamic membership bridge.

Collection empty-check admission must keep receiver identity, collection domain/kind, empty-vs-nonempty predicate direction, threshold/cardinality, and mutation closure beside every length-zero or named-empty bridge.

String prefix/suffix admission must keep string receiver identity, affix coordinate identity, API/import identity, prefix-vs-suffix direction, offset overloads, multi-affix disjunctions, and monkey-patched/custom APIs beside every case-sensitive affix bridge.

cases.claim: Python multi-clause comprehension, nested append loop, and JS flatMap/map compute the same flattened list.
cases.evidence: Focused verify corpus after PR #66: no false merges and complete behavior-equal convergence.

cases.claim: A flattened list is not a nested list of lists.
cases.mutation: FlatMap[A, lambda a. Map[B, lambda b. e]] -> Map[A, lambda a. Map[B, lambda b. e]]
cases.evidence: The #57 equivalence test asserts flat-map and nested-list fingerprints differ.

cases.claim: Mapping to a list without flattening is not one-level flat-map.
cases.mutation: flatMap callback result is kept nested
cases.evidence: Required sibling for any future FlatMap idiom extension.

cases.claim: Literal, factory-backed, imported immutable, and typed dynamic collection membership surfaces can converge when they prove the same searched element and collection receiver/source coordinates.
cases.evidence: The executable replay fixture proves the minimal Python literal membership to JS Set.has bridge; the proof perimeter regression gates cite the broader literal, factory-backed, imported immutable, typed dynamic, and Swift probe membership suites.

cases.claim: Membership over a different searched element is a different proof coordinate even when the collection receiver is identical.
cases.evidence: Literal, typed dynamic, imported, and Set/factory membership tests keep wrong-element fixtures out of the positive membership family.

cases.claim: Membership over different static items, imported providers, or receiver sources changes the collection coordinate.
cases.evidence: The membership suites keep wrong-collection literals, factories, imports, package slices, and local bindings split.

cases.claim: A contains/has/include-shaped call is not collection membership without a proven receiver domain and API identity.
cases.mutation: collection membership API -> substring contains, JavaScript `in`, raw index/count payload, loose equality, missing import, or shadowed factory
cases.evidence: The focused membership tests reject substring receivers, JavaScript `in`, raw indexOf/findIndex/filter length payloads, loose equality predicates, missing imports, shadowed constructors, custom contains receivers, and untyped dynamic `has` calls.

cases.claim: A collection binding mutated after construction/import no longer proves the original membership predicate.
cases.evidence: Module, local, provider, importer, and std-factory mutation fixtures across Python, JS/TS, Go, Java, Ruby, and Rust stay split from the original literal membership family.

cases.claim: Length-zero comparisons and named emptiness predicates converge when they prove the same collection receiver coordinate and empty direction.
cases.evidence: The executable fixture proves the minimal Rust Vec length-zero to is_empty bridge; the proof perimeter regression gates cite broader generated coverage and the Rust/Java CLI empty-check suite.

cases.claim: Negated named emptiness and nonzero length comparisons converge only as the non-empty direction of the same receiver proof.
cases.evidence: The executable fixture records the non-empty direction separately so truthiness/non-emptiness admission cannot be confused with an empty predicate.

cases.claim: A length-one threshold is not strict emptiness, even though it has the same receiver and length surface.
cases.evidence: Generated collection_empty_check negatives and the focused fixture keep zero-length predicates distinct from one-length/cardinality thresholds.

cases.claim: Emptiness over a different collection parameter is a different receiver coordinate.
cases.evidence: Generated wrong-receiver negatives and the focused fixture keep same-shaped emptiness predicates split when the collection coordinate changes.

cases.claim: A collection mutated before the emptiness predicate no longer proves the original receiver state.
cases.mutation: read receiver emptiness -> mutate receiver, then read emptiness
cases.evidence: The focused fixture pins mutation closure so future empty-check expansion cannot treat a stale receiver proof as current state.

cases.claim: Case-sensitive prefix predicates converge across supported receiver/API surfaces when they prove the same string receiver and literal affix coordinate.
cases.evidence: The string_affix_550 CLI fixture proves Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, and Java prefix predicates under exact string receiver, API identity, and literal affix evidence.

cases.claim: Case-sensitive suffix predicates converge when they prove the same string receiver and literal suffix coordinate.
cases.evidence: The string_affix_550 CLI fixture records suffix direction separately from prefix direction.

cases.claim: Same-role parameter affixes converge across supported languages when the receiver and affix parameter coordinates both match.
cases.evidence: The string_affix_552 coordinate fixture proves TypeScript, Swift, and Python parameter affixes when the same parameter role is used.

cases.claim: Direct literal affixes and immutable local/module binding affixes converge when they prove the same affix value coordinate.
cases.evidence: The string_affix_552 coordinate fixture proves immutable literal/local/module binding affixes against direct literal affixes.

cases.claim: Ruby String#start_with? and String#end_with? converge only after literal string receiver proof and standard String API identity are present.
cases.evidence: The Ruby string_affix_551 fixture proves literal string receiver admission for both prefix and suffix directions.

cases.claim: A prefix predicate is not a suffix predicate even when receiver and literal affix coordinates are otherwise compatible.
cases.evidence: The JS/TS/Python and Ruby fixtures keep prefix and suffix directions in separate semantic families.

cases.claim: A string-affix-shaped call without exact string receiver proof, or over a different receiver coordinate, cannot join the proved affix family.
cases.evidence: JS/TS receiver hard negatives and wrong-receiver Rust fixtures remain outside the proved prefix family.

cases.claim: Changing the literal or parameter affix coordinate changes the predicate.
cases.evidence: The coordinate fixture keeps wrong parameter roles and changed literal affixes out of proved affix families.

cases.claim: Derived or mutated affix values are not the same coordinate as the original literal or parameter proof.
cases.mutation: literal/parameter affix -> transformed or mutated affix binding
cases.evidence: The coordinate fixture keeps dynamic parameter transformations and mutated affix bindings outside immutable-coordinate proof.

cases.claim: Offset overloads and tuple/multi-affix disjunctions are not whole-string single-affix predicates until their extra semantics are modeled.
cases.mutation: single whole-string affix -> offset overload or multi-affix disjunction
cases.evidence: JS/Java offset forms may form their own offset family, and Python/Ruby multi-affix forms stay outside the whole-string single-affix proof perimeter.

cases.claim: Ruby same-name custom methods, untyped receivers, wrong receivers, and monkey-patched String APIs do not prove standard String#start_with? identity.
cases.mutation: standard Ruby String affix API -> custom or patched same-name API
cases.evidence: The Ruby fixture keeps custom same-name methods and same-file String monkey patches out of the proved Ruby prefix family.

cases.claim: filter_map-style option-producing callbacks can converge with explicit filter+map where None drops elements.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test and hof_filter_map smoke converge Python filtered comprehension, JS filter().map(), Rust filter_map Some/None, and Rust guarded Vec::new()/push builder.

cases.claim: Dropping None differs from mapping None as a value.
cases.mutation: filter_map callback returns None where map keeps a sentinel value
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test rejects a Rust map that emits Option payloads instead of dropping None.

cases.claim: Changing the mapped Some value changes behavior even when the predicate stays the same.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test rejects Some(x * 3) against the covered Some(x * 2) value coordinate.

cases.claim: filter_map keeps falsey Some-like values; only Null/None absence drops an item.
cases.mutation: coerce the callback result through truthiness before deciding whether to emit it
cases.evidence: Interpreter FilterMap tests keep Int(0), and focused equivalence test converges Some(0) with a filtered zero map while rejecting a later truthy zero filter.

cases.claim: Richer option-producing match/and_then forms may converge with explicit filter+map when they preserve the same absence and emitted-value coordinates.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test and hof_filter_map smoke converge Python/TypeScript filter+map with Rust match-guard and pure Option::and_then filter_map callbacks.

cases.claim: A wrapped None payload is an emitted value in richer option domains, not the current Null absence sentinel.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test converges Rust Some(None) payloads with Python filtered None values and rejects them against mapped x*2 values.

cases.claim: A sum over a flat-map stream equals the corresponding nested reduction loop.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test converges Python sum over a flat-map generator, Python nested reduction loop, and JS flatMap().reduce().

cases.claim: A zero-seeded nested selection loop clamps at its seed (returns 0 on empty or all-negative input); true max over the flat-map stream does not.
cases.evidence: nose verify flagged the previous positive labeling as a false merge (10 differing inputs) once 2-argument min/max became interpretable; selection reductions now key their seed, and the focused equivalence test asserts the fingerprints differ while equal-seeded loops still converge.

cases.claim: An any/existence reduction over a flat-map stream equals the corresponding nested early-return loop.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test converges any(x + y > 0 for x in xs for y in ys) with a nested early-return existence loop.

cases.claim: Changing the reduction seed changes aggregate behavior.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test keeps a nested sum loop seeded with 1 distinct from the flat-map sum seeded with 0.

cases.claim: Aggregating a nested list shape differs from aggregating a flattened stream unless a separate flatten is proven.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test keeps sum over nested list rows distinct from sum over the flattened stream.

cases.claim: Changing the flattened any predicate changes behavior.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test keeps the inverted predicate distinct from the covered > predicate.

cases.claim: A flat-map aggregate whose emitted value ignores the outer element still depends on the outer collection cardinality.
cases.mutation: sum(y for x in xs for y in ys) -> sum(y for y in ys)
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test keeps the outer-ignored flat-map aggregate and nested loop distinct from the direct inner sum.

cases.claim: A filtered flat-map aggregate may converge with an equivalent nested guarded reduction when outer and inner predicates are preserved.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test converges Python filtered flat-map sum, Python nested guarded sum loop, JS filtered flatMap().reduce(), and JS method-terminal .some()/.every() with the equivalent Python filtered any/all generators.

cases.claim: Changing an outer or inner FlatMap aggregate predicate changes behavior.
cases.mutation: outer/inner/terminal predicate changed to a static false predicate while contribution stays the same
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test keeps static-false outer predicates, inner predicates, and method-terminal predicates distinct from the covered filtered FlatMap aggregate.

cases.claim: A filtered FlatMap any/all existence or universal aggregate may converge with the equivalent nested guarded early-return loop.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence test converges Python filtered any/all generators, JS filtered flatMap().some()/every(), and equivalent Python nested guarded early-return loops.

cases.claim: A pure Java Stream.flatMap chain can express the same one-level flat-map as Python multi-clause comprehension.
cases.evidence: Focused Java stream corpus verifies with 4/4 interpretable units, zero false merges, and complete behavior-equal convergence; the source-level equivalence test asserts Java Stream.flatMap/map matches Python multi-clause comprehension.

cases.claim: Java Stream.map returning streams is not Stream.flatMap.
cases.evidence: The focused corpus includes nestedMapJava and nested_map_py as the nested-shape sibling, and the source-level equivalence test asserts nested-map fingerprints differ from flat-map fingerprints.

cases.claim: Effectful stream callbacks cannot be treated as pure HoF transformations.
cases.mutation: lambda mutates external state or performs an effect
cases.evidence: The Java stream oracle tests execute a FlatMap callback containing a print effect and assert the effect trace is preserved, so callback effects remain observable and outside the pure idiom rule.

cases.claim: Clamp-shaped min/max compositions converge when numeric lo<=hi is proven.
cases.evidence: Proof-backed integer min/max compositions now converge through Clamp when an exiting inverse guard or ordered literal bounds prove lo<=hi. Focused smoke: numeric_clamp positive recall 1/1.

cases.claim: Clamp composition is not sound when lo<=hi is not proven.
cases.mutation: remove or invert the bound-order proof
cases.evidence: Focused tests reject missing and non-exiting guards, swapped bounds, wrong nesting, unproven ternary clamps, and unproven Rust .clamp(lo, hi); numeric_clamp smoke reports 0/4 hard-negative false merges and the bridge corpus verifies with 0 false merges.

cases.claim: Floating-point NaN/min/max behavior is not covered by integer clamp facts.
cases.evidence: Float-annotated clamp min/max and ternary forms remain outside the integer Clamp canon; numeric_clamp smoke includes a float boundary hard negative and the bridge corpus verifies with 0 false merges.

cases.claim: A two-comparison clamp can converge with proof-backed min/max clamp composition under the same integer lo<=hi proof.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence tests prove the guarded lower-first Python ternary clamp converges with proof-backed min/max Clamp while unproven, swapped-bound, and float ternaries stay split. The bridge fixture also keeps the upper-first spelling visible as adjacent corpus evidence, not as a broader admission claim.

cases.claim: Language library clamp forms can converge with proof-backed min/max clamp composition when the same integer bound proof is available.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence tests prove literal ordered Rust .clamp converges with literal min/max Clamp, and guarded Rust .clamp converges with guarded Rust x.max(lo).min(hi) under the same lo<=hi proof. The bridge corpus verifies that unproven, custom-method, and float boundaries stay split.

cases.claim: A method named clamp is not a numeric library clamp without a proven numeric receiver and bound-order proof.
cases.mutation: custom receiver method or parameter bounds without lo<=hi proof
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence tests keep unproven Rust x.clamp(lo, hi) and custom Wrap::clamp forms split from literal/proof-backed Clamp values; the bridge corpus verifies with 0 false merges.

cases.claim: A Python all(...) universal predicate can converge with an early-return loop that returns False on the De Morgan counterexample and True after exhaustion.
cases.evidence: The README-shaped positive pair is now detector-admitted under the modeled proof facts: the focused executable expectation requires all_not_zero_or_one and loop_no_zero_or_one to report one semantic family.

cases.claim: Changing the empty-iterable result breaks all(...) vacuous truth.
cases.evidence: The hard-negative fixture includes loop_wrong_empty_truth, which returns False for empty input while all(...) returns True.

cases.claim: Observed predicate or loop-body effects prevent treating the loop and all(...) as pure boolean rewrites.
cases.mutation: insert observed append before the counterexample return
cases.evidence: The hard-negative fixture uses the same `(xs, seen)` signature on both functions; loop_with_observed_effect mutates the seen list, so the split depends on observable effects rather than arity.

cases.claim: Helper calls inside the all(...) predicate remain closed unless a separate purity proof proves they have no observable effects.
cases.mutation: replace the local comparison predicate with is_allowed(x, seen), whose body appends to observed state
cases.evidence: The all(...) form delegates the predicate to is_allowed, and that helper mutates the shared seen list before returning the same boolean comparison.

cases.claim: Python and/or can return operand payloads in value contexts, so this packet's De Morgan step is safe only for boolean-only predicates.
cases.mutation: boolean predicate result is replaced by a value-returning `and` operand
cases.evidence: The hard-negative fixture includes value_returning_operand and marker so future admission must prove boolean-only operands rather than rewriting value-returning `and` payloads.

cases.claim: Changing the De Morgan predicate changes behavior even when the surface still contains != and or.
cases.evidence: The hard-negative fixture includes all_changed_predicate, which is true for every scalar except impossible simultaneous 0 and 1.

cases.claim: The loop and all(...) must consume the same iterable; changing the iterated receiver changes behavior.
cases.mutation: loop iterates ys while all(...) iterates xs
cases.evidence: The hard-negative fixture uses the same `(xs, ys)` signature on both functions but drives the loop from ys, so future admission must prove same-iterator identity instead of matching only predicate shape.

cases.claim: Imported immutable literal map lookup with default can converge with local literal/default forms when provenance is proven.
cases.evidence: Semantic query groups local.py and imported.py after Python sibling import provenance resolves the unmutated literal provider.

cases.claim: Receiver mutation between binding/import and lookup changes behavior.
cases.mutation: insert write to receiver before lookup
cases.evidence: Provider and importer mutation fixtures stay out of the imported/local semantic family across Python and JS imports.

cases.claim: Looking up the same key/default on a different map is behaviorally different.
cases.evidence: Existing map-default tests plus cross-file Python, JS, Java, and Rust wrong-map fixtures keep changed present-key values split.

cases.claim: Imported JavaScript/TypeScript literal map exports can converge with local map-default forms when module/export provenance is proven.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence tests and the map_default_non_python_import corpus prove JS/TS named imports from unmutated sibling map exports converge with local literal map-default lookup.

cases.claim: Imported Java static literal map bindings can converge with local map-default forms when static import provenance is proven.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence tests and the map_default_non_python_import corpus prove Java static imports from unmutated class Map.of fields converge with local literal map-default lookup.

cases.claim: Imported Rust const map-entry arrays can converge with local map-default forms when module/export provenance is proven.
cases.evidence: Focused equivalence tests and the map_default_non_python_import corpus prove Rust use-imported const entry arrays consumed by HashMap::from converge with local literal map-default lookup.

cases.claim: HoF oracle behavior must preserve lambda error propagation and empty-collection behavior.
cases.evidence: Interpreter tests cover Map/Filter/FlatMap/FilterMap lambda errors, empty collections, and FilterMap capture/null behavior; the focused HoF oracle corpus verifies with zero false merges.

cases.claim: FlatMap callback results must be lists; non-list callback results are Err in the oracle.
cases.evidence: Interpreter tests assert scalar FlatMap lambda results are Err; the focused corpus carries a scalar flatMap fixture.

cases.claim: Effectful callbacks cannot be folded into pure value-graph HoF facts without effect modeling.
cases.evidence: Interpreter tests assert FilterMap callback print effects remain observable and ordered; the hof_filter_map corpus carries an effectful Rust filter_map callback that the value graph must leave opaque.

cases.claim: Deep HoF chains should retain compact value fingerprints.
cases.evidence: Generated by query_regression HoF smoke as a 32-step filter/map/reduce chain. The focused smoke measured 527 tokens, 377 value-fingerprint nodes, and 1 return node under budgets of 900 tokens, 450 value nodes, and 12 return nodes; cargo large_generated also asserts the deep chain stays compact and distinct from changed predicates/maps.

cases.claim: Wide generated HoF expressions should not explode value-node count or query runtime.
cases.evidence: Generated by query_regression HoF smoke as 12 summed filter/map/reduce chains of depth 6. The focused smoke measured 1299 tokens, 326 value-fingerprint nodes, and 1 return node under budgets of 1600 tokens, 1200 value nodes, and 12 return nodes; cargo large_generated asserts the same wide shape stays compact.
